signals.evidence: Natalie Kadosh (50): 'The child doesn't leave the hotel room, only when there's an alert. She goes down with the dog to the shelter.'
Natalie Kadosh: 'Rental prices are sky-high, and who wants to rent for one or two months? A day before Passover we received notice to vacate.'
Natalie Kadosh: 'The shelter's toilets in the building got clogged and flooded the shelter, which is full of dirt and waste.'

Finance and Interior Ministries agreed to transfer 100 million shekels to local authorities for emergency expenses during Operation 'Lion's Roar', with additional 50 million if fighting continues after Passover.
Emergency medicine center in Kiryat Shmona closed.
Ministry of Education will allow flexibility on Thursday and Friday next week, with emphasis on emotional dialogue and shelter drills before full return to school in capsules near protected spaces.
Significant decline in ER visits since war outbreak: 12% drop in general ER, 30% drop in pediatric ER, 9% drop in obstetric ER, 17% drop in mental health ER.
Prime Minister Netanyahu promised to fix unemployment benefits framework for private sector workers to receive benefits from first day of current Iran war.
Home Front Command calls public to plan travel routes in advance with clear stopping points for protection, know protected spaces at destination, and update Home Front Command app.
Home Front Command: 'Home Front Command works to save lives and works in partnership with civilians. The enemy wants to harm the home front.'
Public sector workers will receive 1.5% wage increase starting April 2026 salary, as part of July 2023 framework agreement.
Magen David Adom paramedic assisted mother with infant after missile strike in Petah Tikva, helping them exit the street and reach ambulance.
Chagit Yehezkel: 'We went down to the shelter, me, my husband and three children and there was a huge explosion. The shelter door shook, the walls shook.'
Chabad volunteers organizing Passover seders in public shelters and underground parking; over 60,000 meals sent this week to hundreds of seders.
Rabbi Mendi Bloi from Chabad: 'Everyone will be okay. This year we increased the volume of meals for seders more than any year, in prayer and hope that we merit true freedom.'
Lilach (wife of Michael Peretz, wheelchair user): 'I sit and tremble with fear, thinking what's happening to Michael meanwhile. I'm much more afraid this time, with all the explosions and alerts.'
Michael Peretz, wheelchair user in Carmiel, remains outside during alerts unable to reach shelter 12 steps away, curling up on wheelchair to protect his head.
Sergeant R.: 'On one hand it's frustrating, the family wanted us to be with them at home. On the other hand, it's a sense of mission. We're here to be a first line before civilians, to protect them.'
Clalit data: significant decline in ER visits in past month compared to previous month—general ER down, pediatric ER down, obstetric ER down, mental health ER down.

Thousands want to volunteer to help on home front but fear alerts; 'Good Spirit' organization offers remote volunteering options including phone calls to elderly, mental health content creation, and online activities.
Over 20% increase in women at risk seeking help from 'Turning the Creators' organization since war began; women in rehabilitation fear losing progress made with great effort.

Rambam Hospital: 4 casualties from southern Lebanon fighting brought to trauma room; one severely wounded underwent surgery, condition improved and stable; 17 soldiers currently hospitalized, all stable.
Begin Heritage Center, museums, and attractions operating during Passover holiday with protected spaces and activities adapted to emergency guidelines.

Senior military official: 'We are determined to continue and achieve victories. We are a month into the campaign—a complex period for civilians—and I want to express appreciation for the resilience the public is demonstrating.'

300% increase in Bedouin women volunteers for national service; security system invested nearly 75 million shekels in service members over 3 years for economic resilience and academic/employment advancement.

Paramedic Fadi Hamdan: 'I noticed a woman with a baby near burning vehicles. She was very distressed and struggled to lift the baby. She handed him to me and I helped them exit and move away from the thick smoke.'
Supreme Court rejected petition for immediate private access to public shelter; Disability Equality Commissioner working with municipality with target resolution by May 2, 2026.
Hiriya recycling park in central region offers protected spaces for drivers on Highway 4 during alerts; signage directs drivers to shelter.
Health Ministry preparing for mass casualty event scenario in Eilat; recruiting volunteer doctors via registration form to ensure rapid response capability.

Boaz, northern resident: 'We will celebrate the holiday at home, that's a decision we made. We expect to be eight people around the holiday table, but even the simplest preparations were done in fear.'
Boaz: 'If they evacuate again—this time I wouldn't leave.'
Psychometric exams in adapted conditions scheduled for April 10, 2026 postponed due to security situation; alternative date not set before April 26, 2026.

Local authorities dispute Education Ministry guidance on resuming physical learning in small groups; disagreement over terminology ('capsules'), capacity limits, and feasibility of finding enough protected spaces.
Alerts activated in Gush Dan, Sharon, Shephelah, and Samaria following Iranian missile fire; public instructed to remain in protected spaces pending all-clear.

Knesset approved law for rehabilitation of areas damaged in Operation 'Lion's Roar' through urban renewal; expands planning committee powers, eases majority requirements, allows residents enhanced cash compensation for immediate alternative housing.

Rakhshei Lev organization holding Passover seders for cancer patients, families, and medical teams in central hospitals; distributing food baskets and meal vouchers to patient families; providing meals to medical teams in protected facilities.
New initiative launching at Mount Meron to identify at-risk youth; dedicated outreach vehicle and trained teams will build trust and mediate connection to care and rehabilitation services.

IDF completed Passover preparations across all sectors with full nutritional and halakhic provisions adapted to field conditions and multiple scenarios, coordinated by Technology & Logistics Division and Military Rabbinate.
Moran Fider, age 31: 'I felt tremendous pressure in my head, I couldn't feel my hands. Suddenly I felt like I was looking at the world from inside a ship rocking in a storm.'

Guidance provided: plan travel in advance, avoid traffic, check for protected spaces per Home Front Command instructions; knowing what to do in case of alert reduces stress for both parents and children
Senior Home Front Command official: 'we need to be outside, strong, ready because we haven't always been right in our assessments and we don't take risks'
Home Front Command: defensive policy will remain unchanged; gatherings permitted: 50 people in orange zones near protected space, 100 in yellow zones near standard protected space

Mother of two toddlers: 'private daycare centers are closed, payments continue, and there is no solution in sight. Without childcare frameworks, it is impossible to maintain a stable economy in the country'
Thousands of parents with young children remain without childcare framework; private daycare centers closed; no agreed framework; no compensation visible
Home Front Command: install app to receive alerts during holiday travel; alerts not always audible from sirens
Ministry of Education preparing return to studies in 'capsules' — rotating age groups or classes attending school on different days, combining in-person and Zoom learning
IDF Spokesperson Efi Defrin: 'The situation is unbearable for us' — shortage of 12,000-15,000 soldiers, including ~7,000 combat troops
IDF Spokesperson: 'We need legislation for military conscription to bring soldiers to the IDF' and to extend regular service from 30 to 36 months
Grandfather of injured children at Soroka Hospital, when told children could go home: 'They don't have a home'
Ahavat Torah movement: daily Zoom learning with thousands of children participating; response described as enthusiastic and strengthening
Israel Shila, Deputy Director of Education, Ahavat Torah: 'We became an anchor of belonging and learning for many children in this period — we see this as a great privilege and binding mission'
Cave of the Patriarchs management announced: the site will be closed during Passover; restrictions are among the most severe since the start of the campaign

Prime Minister held emergency meeting with Chamber of Commerce president regarding unemployment benefits framework discrimination; committed to meet Finance Minister next morning to correct the framework before Passover
Chabad 'Lev Chabad' project: organizing 1,300 public Seders for 50,000 people in parking lots and underground shelters; over 4,000 families of terror victims received matzah kits and support

Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Aharonov, head of Chabad Youth: 'Even in wartime, we are preparing so that those in hospitals will celebrate Passover with a homey and festive feeling. We also organized a unique activity for half a million children'

Chabad Emissaries Fund granted special grant to ~1,500 Chabad emissaries in Israel organizing thousands of public Seders at high cost; grant funded by donors to ease holiday expenses for emissary families in combat and evacuation zones

Education Ministry directing schools to prepare for return to in-person learning in 'capsules' after Passover; kindergarten, grades 1-2, and high school students (for exams) to return first; target: at least three days per week in-person with hybrid learning
Football League management: Ramat Hasharon Stadium (Ashdod) approved for matches after installation of 2 portable shelters; only Doha Stadium in Sakhnin remains unapproved

Hadassah hospitals: transferred most hospitalized patients to underground protected compartments; converted underground parking lots to accommodate hundreds of non-mobile patients; required intensive infrastructure work for ventilation, electricity, water, sanitation, medical staffing
Hadassah Ein Kerem: operating rooms in basement (prepared over a decade ago) continue functioning without interruption during alerts; surgical teams continue operating without need for evacuation

Megiddo Regional Council: all hiking trails, streams, and nature areas closed throughout Passover and intermediate days due to missile impact and Home Front Command directives; no shelter available in open areas

IDF Technology and Logistics Division: delivering hot Passover meals to forward positions and assembly areas; new 'Matzva' and 'Chai'r Board' packages adapted for combat conditions; first-time allowance of legumes for all combat troops; special provisions for vegetarians, vegans, and gluten-sensitive soldiers

IDF: operating dedicated emergency hotline during Passover to resolve dietary and logistical issues in real time; ensuring every soldier in field receives hot meal on Seder night within operational constraints
Ministry of Health: healthcare system operating in heightened readiness mode; hospitals continuing to receive patients while maintaining treatment continuity across all directions
Ministry directs non-life-threatening cases to urgent care centers rather than hospital ERs to reduce ER load and accelerate treatment of severe patients
Ministry emphasizes psychological support available through support centers and hospital hotlines for residents experiencing anxiety, stress, or trauma
National Road Safety Authority: 26 deaths in 89 traffic accidents since war began (Feb 28); security situation increasingly influencing driver behavior and road danger levels
IDF Home Front Command: no plans to change wartime guidelines; restrictions on large gatherings and educational activities remain in effect
Wizz Air extends flight suspension through April 20; Ben Gurion Airport closed to foreign airlines since Feb 28
Arik, book seller at Geula Avenue: 'life continues as usual, and people are out if there is no war'; most stores operating normally despite travel restrictions elsewhere
Center Jerusalem stores (Mahane Yehuda market) experiencing economic disaster; overseas tourist revenues comprise over 50% of sales; near-complete stoppage of travel during peak shopping season
Government announces NIS 100 million to regional councils for wartime expenses; additional amounts allocated as campaign continues; funds ensure functional continuity and essential services
Israel Innovation Authority: nearly half of tech firms struggling with worker shortages; thousands on reserve duty; schools closed; fatigue from constant shelter alerts
Air France extends flight suspension through April 19; Ben Gurion Airport closed to foreign airlines due to security situation
Father of Maxsim Entis at funeral: 'My son is a hero, but I don't want a hero for a son. I want my son at home... You came back, but only in a coffin'
20,000 new immigrants arrived in Israel in past 11 months; includes 4,119 children/teens and 2,426 people over 65
Latet pre-Passover report: 52.6% of Israelis fear economic deterioration or already experiencing financial distress; economic pressure now shared across large parts of society
Father of Maxsim Entis at funeral: 'I have a heroic son, but I don't want a heroic son. I want a son at home... You came back - but in a coffin'
Brother Uri of Capt. Noam Madmoni at funeral: 'I had planned for you to officiate at my wedding in two months - and now I am eulogizing you over your grave'
Adeena Sussman: Israelis running to bomb shelters for protection from deadly Iranian missile attacks; prospect of hosting Passover meals feels overwhelming
Adeena Sussman: becoming immersed in kitchen activities during wartime 'can be a little bit of an escape'; running informal WarBnB cooking for friends/family lacking bomb shelters
IDF commanders demanded reservists with psychological injuries and PTSD report for duty; threatened arrest for non-compliance despite soldiers explaining mental health conditions
Air raid sirens sounded across central Israel; millions sent to shelter; Home Front Command later allowed residents to leave protected spaces after interceptions identified
Sarit about husband Eliav in Lebanon: 'The children don't get used to the fact that dad isn't home... They keep asking why he's leaving again and when he'll be back'
Sarit: 'We have no certainty about him. The last time we spoke was last week, and since then I've only received updates through representatives saying everything is OK'
Maxsim's siblings: 'His message to the world was, Everything is OK, no matter how hard it is. He would walk into a room and immediately spread his light and energy'
Hezbollah launched multiple rocket barrages; repeated air-raid sirens across Haifa, Krayot, Galilee; two people treated for anxiety; no physical injuries reported
Ministry of Finance, Interior, and Local Authority Center agreed: municipalities receive 100 million shekels for wartime expenses; additional 50 million if war continues through Passover

Ayala Ben Harosh, 57, from Nahariya: 'I immediately experience bouts of crying and shaking, a feeling like I'm about to have a heart attack, and the crying just doesn't stop. It has changed my life, made it unbearable.'
More than 38,000 have sought mental health help since the Iran war began, but officials warn this is only the tip of the iceberg.

Knesset approved furlough framework for Operation Roaring Lion; employees on furlough eligible for unemployment benefits from tenth day; qualifying period shortened from 18 months to 6 months; payment from first day.

Adi (brother of Staff Sergeant Maxsim Entis): 'Maxim always said the people of Israel are one. Attend the funerals, visit the hospitals. Stand with the families even if you didn't know them. We are one family.'

MDA emergency medic Meir Biton: 'We found the worker lying conscious with injuries to his lower limbs. He told us he had been hit by shrapnel while working. We treated him on site and evacuated him by intensive care ambulance to the hospital.'

Lieutenant Colonel Ortal Gavish, head of Food Distribution Department, IDF General Staff Supply Center: 'We at the General Staff Supply Center have been preparing for Passover for a long time. At around July-August, we begin preparing for Passover. The work includes a framework for those in mess halls and those who are away from a kitchen, with special field rations for the holiday.'
IDF Spokesman Effie Defrin: 'The IDF had no warning of the massive missile barrage from Lebanon' despite sirens being activated continuously across northern communities.
